sanskrit: visṛjya tu suhṛdvargaṃ buddhyā niścitya rāghavaḥ samīpe dvāḥstham āsīnam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having dismissed the company of friends and resolved in his mind, Rāghava spoke these words to the doorkeeper who was seated nearby.

sanskrit: śīghram ānaya saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam bharataṃ ca mahābāhuṃ śatrughnaṃ cāparājitam
english: "Quickly bring Saumitri Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks, and the long-armed Bharata, and the unconquered Śatrughna."

sanskrit: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ lakṣmaṇasya gṛhaṃ gatvā praviveśānivāritaḥ
english: Having heard Rāma's command, the doorkeeper placed his joined palms upon his head and went to Lakṣmaṇa's house, entering without obstruction.

sanskrit: uvāca ca tadā vākyaṃ vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ draṣṭum icchati rājā tvāṃ gamyatāṃ tatra mā ciram
english: And then he spoke with joined palms raised in salutation: "The king desires to see you; go there without delay."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva saumitriḥ śrutvā rāghavaśāsanam prādravad ratham āruhya rāghavasya niveśanam
english: "Indeed, so be it" — hearing Rāghava's command, Saumitri mounted his chariot and hastened to Rāghava's dwelling.

sanskrit: prayāntaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā dvāḥstho bharatam antikāt uvāca prāñjalir vākyaṃ rājā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati
english: Seeing Lakṣmaṇa depart, the doorkeeper approached Bharata nearby and said with joined palms: "The king desires to see you."

sanskrit: bharatas tu vacaḥ śrutvā dvāḥsthād rāmasamīritam utpapātāsanāt tūrṇaṃ padbhyām eva tato 'gamat
english: But Bharata, hearing the word of Rāma conveyed by the doorkeeper, leapt up swiftly from his seat and went there on foot.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā prayāntaṃ bharataṃ tvaramāṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ śatrughnabhavanaṃ gatvā tato vākyaṃ jagāda ha
english: Seeing Bharata departing, the doorkeeper hastened with joined palms to Śatrughna's residence and spoke these words.

sanskrit: ehy āgaccha raghuśreṣṭha rājā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati gato hi lakṣmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ bharataś ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: "Come, O best of the Raghus, the king desires to see you; for Lakṣmaṇa has already gone, and so has the greatly renowned Bharata."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya śatrughno rāmaśāsanam śirasā vandya dharaṇīṃ prayayau yatra rāghavaḥ
english: Hearing that message — the command of Rāma — Śatrughna bowed his head to the ground in reverence and went to where Rāghava was.

sanskrit: kumārān āgatāñ śrutvā cintāvyākulitendriyaḥ avākśirā dīnamanā dvāḥsthaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing that the princes had arrived, with his faculties disturbed by anguish, his head bowed low and his mind dejected, Rāma spoke to the doorkeeper.

sanskrit: praveśaya kumārāṃs tvaṃ matsamīpaṃ tvarānvitaḥ eteṣu jīvitaṃ mahyam ete prāṇā bahiścarāḥ
english: "Bring the princes quickly to my presence; my life resides in them — they are my vital breaths that walk abroad."

sanskrit: ājñaptās tu narendreṇa kumārāḥ śuklavāsasaḥ prahvāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā viviśus te samāhitāḥ
english: Thus directed by the lord of men, the princes, clad in white garments, entered humbly with joined palms, composed and attentive.

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ tasya sagrahaṃ śaśinaṃ yathā saṃdhyāgatam ivādityaṃ prabhayā parivarjitam
english: But they, seeing his face like the moon in eclipse, like the sun at dusk stripped of its radiance,

sanskrit: bāṣpapūrṇe ca nayane dṛṣṭvā rāmasya dhīmataḥ hataśobhaṃ yathā padmaṃ mukhaṃ vīkṣya ca tasya te
english: and beholding the tear-filled eyes of wise Rāma, and seeing his face like a lotus bereft of its beauty —

sanskrit: tato 'bhivādya tvaritāḥ pādau rāmasya mūrdhabhiḥ tasthuḥ samāhitāḥ sarve rāmaś cāśrūṇy avartayat
english: — they then quickly bowed their heads to Rāma's feet in obeisance and all stood composed, while Rāma shed tears.

sanskrit: tān pariṣvajya bāhubhyām utthāpya ca mahābhujaḥ āsaneṣv ādhvam ity uktvā tato vākyaṃ jagāda ha
english: The mighty-armed one embraced them with both arms, raised them up, said "Be seated," and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: bhavanto mama sarvasvaṃ bhavanto mama jīvitam bhavadbhiś ca kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ pālayāmi nareśvarāḥ
english: "You are my all, you are my life; it is by you that this kingdom has been made, and I now protect it, O lords of men.

sanskrit: bhavantaḥ kṛtaśāstrārthā buddhau ca pariniṣṭhitāḥ saṃbhūya ca madartho 'yam anveṣṭavyo nareśvarāḥ
english: "You are well-versed in the meaning of the śāstras and thoroughly grounded in discernment; together you must seek out this matter that concerns me, O lords of men."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samupaviṣṭānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dīnacetasām uvāca vākyaṃ kākutstho mukhena pariśuṣyatā
english: When they had all sat down, their hearts full of sorrow, Kākutstha spoke with a parched face.

sanskrit: sarve śṛṇuta bhadraṃ vo mā kurudhvaṃ mano 'nyathā paurāṇāṃ mama sītāyāṃ yādṛśī vartate kathā
english: "All of you listen, blessings upon you; do not turn your minds otherwise. Regarding Sītā, such is the report that circulates among the citizens toward me:

sanskrit: paurāpavādaḥ sumahāṃs tathā janapadasya ca vartate mayi bībhatsaḥ sa me marmāṇi kṛntati
english: "A very great reproach from the townspeople and likewise from the countryside is directed at me — a hateful reproach that cuts into my very vitals.

sanskrit: ahaṃ kila kule jāto ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām sītāṃ pāpasamācārām ānayeyaṃ kathaṃ pure
english: "'He is born in the lineage of the great-souled Ikṣvākus — how could he bring back to his city a Sītā of wicked conduct?'

sanskrit: jānāsi hi yathā saumya daṇḍake vijane vane rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā sa ca vidhvaṃsito mayā
english: "For you know, dear Saumitri, how Sītā was abducted by Rāvaṇa in the desolate forest of Daṇḍaka, and how he was destroyed by me.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ tava saumitre devānāṃ havyavāhanaḥ apāpāṃ maithilīm āha vāyuś cākāśagocaraḥ
english: "Before your very eyes, O Saumitri, Havyavāhana — the fire of the gods — and Vāyu who moves through the sky declared that Maithilī was without sin.

sanskrit: candrādityau ca śaṃsete surāṇāṃ saṃnidhau purā ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva sarveṣām apāpāṃ janakātmajām
english: "And Candra and Āditya too testified in the presence of all the gods and all the seers, long ago, that the daughter of Janaka was blameless.

sanskrit: evaṃ śuddhasamācārā devagandharvasaṃnidhau laṅkādvīpe mahendreṇa mama haste niveśitā
english: "She thus certified as pure in conduct was placed into my hand by great Indra on the island of Laṅkā, in the presence of gods and gandharvas.

sanskrit: antarātmā ca me vetti sītāṃ śuddhāṃ yaśasvinīm tato gṛhītvā vaidehīm ayodhyām aham āgataḥ
english: "And my inner soul knows Sītā to be pure and illustrious. Having taken Vaidehī back, I came to Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu me mahān vādaḥ śokaś ca hṛdi vartate paurāpavādaḥ sumahāṃs tathā janapadasya ca
english: "Yet this great dispute and grief remains in my heart — the very great reproach of the citizens and of the countryside alike.

sanskrit: akīrtir yasya gīyeta loke bhūtasya kasya cit pataty evādhamāṃl lokān yāvac chabdaḥ sa kīrtyate
english: "Any being in this world of whom infamy is sung falls into the lowest realms for as long as that report is remembered.

sanskrit: akīrtir nindyate daivaiḥ kīrtir deveṣu pūjyate kīrtyarthaṃ ca samārambhaḥ sarva eva mahātmanām
english: "Infamy is condemned by the divine ones; glory is honoured among the gods; and every undertaking of great-souled persons is for the sake of glory.

sanskrit: apy ahaṃ jīvitaṃ jahyāṃ yuṣmān vā puruṣarṣabhāḥ apavādabhayād bhītaḥ kiṃ punar janakātmajām
english: "I would even abandon my life, or abandon you, O bulls among men, out of fear of disgrace — how much more then the daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: tasmād bhavantaḥ paśyantu patitaṃ śokasāgare na hi paśyāmy ahaṃ bhūyaḥ kiṃ cid duḥkham ato 'dhikam
english: "Therefore let all of you behold me fallen into an ocean of grief; for I see no sorrow greater than this.

sanskrit: śvas tvaṃ prabhāte saumitre sumantrādhiṣṭhitaṃ ratham āruhya sītām āropya viṣayānte samutsṛja
english: "Tomorrow at dawn, O Saumitri, mount the chariot driven by Sumantra, take Sītā aboard, and abandon her at the border of the realm.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyās tu pare pāre vālmīkeḥ sumahātmanaḥ āśramo divyasaṃkāśas tamasātīram āśritaḥ
english: "On the far bank of the Gaṅgā, the hermitage of the greatly noble Vālmīki, divine in its appearance, is situated on the bank of the Tamasā river.

sanskrit: tatraināṃ vijane kakṣe visṛjya raghunandana śīghram āgaccha saumitre kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama
english: "There, in a lonely forest thicket, abandon her, O Raghunandana, and return quickly, O Saumitri — carry out my command.

sanskrit: na cāsmi prativaktavyaḥ sītāṃ prati kathaṃ cana aprītiḥ paramā mahyaṃ bhavet tu prativārite
english: "And I am not to be spoken to in any manner concerning Sītā; my displeasure would be extreme if I were opposed in this.

sanskrit: śāpitāś ca mayā yūyaṃ bhujābhyāṃ jīvitena ca ye māṃ vākyāntare brūyur anunetuṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "And I adjure you by my arms and my life: whoever would speak to dissuade me or seek to placate me in any manner —

sanskrit: mānayantu bhavanto māṃ yadi macchāsane sthitāḥ ito 'dya nīyatāṃ sītā kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama
english: "— let them show me honour only if they abide by my command. From here today let Sītā be taken; carry out my command.

sanskrit: pūrvam ukto 'ham anayā gaṅgātīre mahāśramān paśyeyam iti tasyāś ca kāmaḥ saṃvartyatām ayam
english: "She had formerly expressed to me a wish to visit the great hermitages along the Gaṅgā's bank; let this desire of hers also be fulfilled."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu kākutstho bāṣpeṇa pihitekṣaṇaḥ praviveśa sa dharmātmā bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Kākutstha — that righteous soul — with eyes closed by tears, withdrew and entered, surrounded by his brothers.

sanskrit: tato rajanyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ sumantram abravīd vākyaṃ mukhena pariśuṣyatā
english: Then, when the night had passed, Lakṣmaṇa, his heart dejected, spoke to Sumantra with a parched face.

sanskrit: sārathe turagāñ śīghraṃ yojayasva rathottame svāstīrṇaṃ rājabhavanāt sītāyāś cāsanaṃ śubham
english: "O charioteer, quickly yoke the horses to the finest chariot, well-spread with cushions, and bring also a beautiful seat from the royal palace for Sītā."

sanskrit: sītā hi rājabhavanād āśramaṃ puṇyakarmaṇām mayā neyā maharṣīṇāṃ śīghram ānīyatāṃ rathaḥ
english: "For Sītā must be taken by me from the royal palace to the hermitage of the holy-actioned great seers; let the chariot be brought quickly."

sanskrit: sumantras tu tathety uktvā yuktaṃ paramavājibhiḥ rathaṃ suruciraprakhyaṃ svāstīrṇaṃ sukhaśayyayā
english: Sumantra, saying "So be it," brought the chariot yoked with the finest horses — a chariot gleaming most beautifully, its floor spread soft for comfort.

sanskrit: ādāyovāca saumitriṃ mitrāṇāṃ harṣavardhanam ratho 'yaṃ samanuprāpto yat kāryaṃ kriyatāṃ prabho
english: Having brought it, he said to Saumitri — the increaser of joy among friends — "The chariot stands ready, my lord; let whatever must be done be done."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sumantreṇa rājaveśma sa lakṣmaṇaḥ praviśya sītām āsādya vyājahāra nararṣabhaḥ
english: Addressed thus by Sumantra, that bull among men, Lakṣmaṇa, entered the royal palace, approached Sītā, and spoke.

sanskrit: gaṅgātīre mayā devi munīnām āśrame śubhe śīghraṃ gatvopaneyāsi śāsanāt pārthivasya naḥ
english: "O goddess, you must be brought quickly to the auspicious hermitage of the sages on the bank of the Gaṅgā by me — by command of our lord the king."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu vaidehī lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe gamanaṃ cābhyarocayat
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, Vaidehī experienced incomparable delight and consented gladly to the journey.

sanskrit: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca gṛhītvā tāni vaidehī gamanāyopacakrame
english: Taking precious garments and various jewels, Vaidehī made ready for departure.

sanskrit: imāni munipatnīnāṃ dāsyāmy ābharaṇāny aham saumitris tu tathety uktvā ratham āropya maithilīm prayayau śīghraturago rāmasyājñām anusmaran
english: "These ornaments I shall give to the wives of the sages." Saumitri said "So be it," and having helped Maithilī mount the chariot, set forth with swift horses, bearing in mind Rāma's command.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā sītā lakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmivardhanam aśubhāni bahūny adya paśyāmi raghunandana
english: And then Sītā said to Lakṣmaṇa, the increaser of prosperity: "I see many ill omens today, O Raghunandana.

sanskrit: nayanaṃ me sphuraty adya gātrotkampaś ca jāyate hṛdayaṃ caiva saumitre asvastham iva lakṣaye
english: "My eye throbs today, trembling arises throughout my limbs, and my heart, O Saumitri, I perceive to be unwell.

sanskrit: autsukyaṃ paramaṃ cāpi adhṛtiś ca parā mama śūnyām iva ca paśyāmi pṛthivīṃ pṛthulocana
english: "And my anxiety is extreme, my restlessness profound; the earth itself, O wide-eyed one, I see as though it were empty.

sanskrit: api svasti bhavet tasya bhrātus te bhrātṛbhiḥ saha śvaśrūṇāṃ caiva me vīra sarvāsām aviśeṣataḥ
english: "May all be well with that brother of yours together with his brothers, and likewise with all of my mothers-in-law without exception, O hero.

sanskrit: pure janapade caiva kuśalaṃ prāṇinām api ity añjalikṛtā sītā devatā abhyayācata
english: "And may all living beings in city and countryside likewise be well." So praying, Sītā made the añjali gesture toward the deities.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇo 'rthaṃ tu taṃ śrutvā śirasā vandya maithilīm śivam ity abravīd dhṛṣṭo hṛdayena viśuṣyatā
english: Lakṣmaṇa, hearing that meaning, bowed his head in reverence to Maithilī and said "All will be auspicious" — outwardly composed but with his heart drying up within.

sanskrit: tato vāsam upāgamya gomatītīra āśrame prabhāte punar utthāya saumitriḥ sūtam abravīt
english: Then, having halted for the night at a hermitage on the bank of the Gomatī, Saumitri rose again at dawn and addressed the charioteer.

sanskrit: yojayasva rathaṃ śīghram adya bhāgīrathījalam śirasā dhārayiṣyāmi tryambakaḥ parvate yathā
english: "Yoke the chariot quickly; today I shall bear the waters of the Bhāgīrathī upon my head, as the Three-Eyed Lord bears the river on the mountain."

sanskrit: so 'śvān vicārayitvāśu rathe yuktvā manojavān ārohasveti vaidehīṃ sūtaḥ prāñjalir abravīt
english: Having quickly seen to the horses and yoked those swift-as-thought steeds to the chariot, the charioteer said to Vaidehī with joined palms: "Please mount."

sanskrit: sā tu sūtasya vacanād āruroha rathottamam sītā saumitriṇā sārdhaṃ sumantreṇa ca dhīmatā
english: At the charioteer's words, Sītā mounted the finest chariot together with Saumitri and the wise Sumantra.

sanskrit: athārdhadivasaṃ gatvā bhāgīrathyā jalāśayam nirīkṣya lakṣmaṇo dīnaḥ praruroda mahāsvanam
english: Then, having traveled half a day and glimpsing the waters of the Bhāgīrathī, Lakṣmaṇa, overcome with grief, broke into loud weeping.

sanskrit: sītā tu paramāyattā dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇam āturam uvāca vākyaṃ dharmajña kim idaṃ rudyate tvayā
english: Sītā, utterly devoted, seeing Lakṣmaṇa distressed, addressed him: "O knower of dharma, why do you weep like this?"

sanskrit: jāhnavītīram āsādya cirābhilaṣitaṃ mama harṣakāle kim arthaṃ māṃ viṣādayasi lakṣmaṇa
english: "Having arrived at the bank of the Jāhnavī — long desired by me — why do you cause me distress at a moment of joy, O Lakṣmaṇa?

sanskrit: nityaṃ tvaṃ rāmapādeṣu vartase puruṣarṣabha kaccid vinākṛtas tena dvirātre śokam āgataḥ
english: "You always abide at Rāma's feet, O bull among men — have you perhaps come to grief at being separated from him for two nights?

sanskrit: mamāpi dayito rāmo jīvitenāpi lakṣmaṇa na cāham evaṃ śocāmi maivaṃ tvaṃ bāliśo bhava
english: "Rāma is dear to me too, even more than life, O Lakṣmaṇa — yet I do not grieve so; do not be so childish.

sanskrit: tārayasva ca māṃ gaṅgāṃ darśayasva ca tāpasān tato dhanāni vāsāṃsi dāsyāmy ābharaṇāni ca
english: "Take me across the Gaṅgā and show me the ascetics; then I shall give them wealth, garments, and ornaments.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtvā maharṣīṇāṃ yathārham abhivādanam tatra caikāṃ niśām uṣya yāsyāmas tāṃ purīṃ punaḥ
english: "Then, having paid appropriate homage to the great seers, spending one night there, we shall return to that city."

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā pramṛjya nayane śubhe titīrṣur lakṣmaṇo gaṅgāṃ śubhāṃ nāvam upāharat
english: Having heard her words, wiping her beautiful eyes, Lakṣmaṇa, wishing to cross the blessed Gaṅgā, brought a boat.
